=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- scripts/orchestrate_force_tick.sh:198-214 | severity=high | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, minimax_minimax-m2_5, moonshotai_kimi-k2_5, x-ai_grok-4_20]
  PROBLEM: The fallback infers `TRACKING_ISSUE` from the sub-issue body using a brittle marker, so phase-end callers that pass a sub-issue number can end up with `TRACKING_ISSUE` empty and the force-tick no-op.
  WHY: When the body lacks the exact tracking marker, the script exits 0 with `No tracking issue resolved for force-tick dispatch; skipping.`, so the orchestrator poller never wakes and the fast-follow tick is lost.
- scripts/orchestrate_force_tick.sh:191-194 | severity=medium | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, minimax_minimax-m2_5, moonshotai_kimi-k2_5, x-ai_grok-4_20]
  PROBLEM: `FORCE_TICK_ENABLED=false` exits 0 without persisting any state, so re-enabling within the same cooldown window loses the suppression record.
  WHY: The disable flag is not durable across invocations, so toggling it off and back on inside the same window allows a duplicate dispatch.
- scripts/orchestrate_force_tick.sh:267-318 | severity=high | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, minimax_minimax-m2_5, moonshotai_kimi-k2_5, x-ai_grok-4_20]
  PROBLEM: The claim-then-verify cooldown gate has a TOCTOU window and no atomic compare-and-swap, so two concurrent phase-end runs can both dispatch the poller.
  WHY: The git-backed ai-memory claim/re-read flow can race, letting multiple workflows observe no cooldown and violate the per-tracking-issue idempotency contract.
- scripts/memory_helpers.sh:554-567, 670-685 | severity=medium | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m2_5, moonshotai_kimi-2_5]
  PROBLEM: `memory_force_tick_get` and `memory_force_tick_put` return `ok: true` on transient Git/clone/push failures, so fail-open telemetry looks like a normal cache miss.
  WHY: Callers in `orchestrate_force_tick.sh` treat those failures as "continue without cooldown," which allows duplicate immediate dispatches.
- .github/workflows/review_autofix.yml:838-846, 5451-5463, 6453-6465 | severity=medium | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m2_5, moonshotai_kimi-k2_5, x-ai_grok-4_20]
  PROBLEM: The new force-tick steps assume the `.codex-workflow-src` checkout succeeded and that `orchestrate_force_tick.sh` is present, but the checkout is allowed to fail and the step has no corresponding guard.
  WHY: When the support checkout is missing, the helper is skipped or invoked from a nonexistent path, so the fast-track tick silently disappears on the very paths meant to keep the orchestrator in sync.
- scripts/render_prompt.sh:1-81 | severity=high | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, minimax_minimax-m2_5, moonshotai_kimi-2_5, x-ai_grok-4_20]
  PROBLEM: The new bash renderer only does placeholder substitution plus a grep for three hardcoded placeholders, so the `render_prompt.py` contract checks for required, forbidden, and unknown variables are no longer enforced.
  WHY: Missing required vars or forbidden vars now reach the LLM instead of failing fast, and contract violations outside those three names silently pass through.
- scripts/render_prompt.sh:54, 57 | severity=low | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro]
  PROBLEM: `${SEMBLE_PREFETCH_BLOCK%$'\n'}` and `${SERENA_TOOL_HINTS_BLOCK%$'\n'}` strip only the last trailing newline from multiline content.
  WHY: Multi-paragraph prefetch blocks lose a separator blank line compared to the old renderer, changing prompt layout and section boundaries.
- scripts/render_prompt.sh:32-80 | severity=low | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro]
  PROBLEM: The self-contained bash renderer no longer delegates to `render_prompt.py`, leaving the old shim/documentation relationship stale.
  WHY: Future maintainers can believe the Python contract validation is still active when it is not, and `render_prompt.py` can rot unnoticed.
- scripts/orchestrate_force_tick.sh:305-327 | severity=low | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [moonshotai_kimi-k2_5]
  PROBLEM: The `dispatch_status="failed"` / `memory_force_tick_put(..., "failed")` path and associated telemetry are not exercised because the mock never returns non-zero from `gh workflow run`.
  WHY: Failure modes such as rate limits, missing tokens, or unknown workflow names remain untested.
=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

=== CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===
- requirement: "Keep the matching listed workflow-template wrappers in sync where this issue already names them."
  expected_change_site: workflow-templates/ai-implement.yml, workflow-templates/ai-review.yml, workflow-templates/ai-validate.yml
  confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, minimax_minimax-m2_5, moonshotai_kimi-2_5, x-ai_grok-4_20]
  EVIDENCE: No modifications were made under workflow-templates/; the wrappers are thin `workflow_call` delegates to `.github/workflows/implement.yml`, `.github/workflows/review_autofix.yml`, and `.github/workflows/validate.yml` at `@stable`.
- requirement: "Force-tick dispatch is idempotent per tracking issue within the cooldown window." / "Store cooldown state through `scripts/memory_helpers.sh`."
  expected_change_site: scripts/orchestrate_force_tick.sh, scripts/memory_helpers.sh
  confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [x-ai_grok-4_20]
  EVIDENCE: The implementation uses a git-push-based claim pattern with a TOCTOU window between `memory_force_tick_put` and `memory_force_tick_get`, there is no atomic compare-and-swap, and `FORCE_TICK_ENABLED=false` exits without persisting state.
- requirement: "Tests cover cooldown/no-op behavior and the dispatch payload shape."
  expected_change_site: tests/test_orchestrate_force_tick.py
  confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, minimax_minimax-m2_5, moonshotai_kimi-2_5, x-ai_grok-4_20]
  EVIDENCE: The test file covers the happy path and sequential cooldown/no-op behavior, but not `FORCE_TICK_ENABLED=false`, failed Git push to ai-memory, failed `gh workflow run` / `dispatch_status=failed`, resolver-failed, or a genuine concurrent race.
=== END CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===

=== FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===
- File: scripts/render_prompt.sh
  Line or code reference: Lines 46-81 (entire substitution loop) — the removal of `exec python3 render_prompt.py` delegation
  Problem: The old `render_prompt.py` enforced per-mode YAML contracts (`required_vars`, `forbidden_vars`, `optional_vars` defaults). The new bash renderer performs only string substitution and a post-render grep check for unresolved `{{WORKFLOW_EDIT_RESTRICTION}}`, `{{SEMBLE_PREFETCH}}`, and `{{SERENA_TOOL_HINTS}}` placeholders; it does not validate any other forbidden vars, required vars, or optional defaults defined in the contract YAML files.
  Why it fails at runtime: If a prompt template is misconstructed, the LLM receives a prompt with unreplaced or incorrectly present content rather than the workflow failing fast.
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5
- File: scripts/orchestrate_force_tick.sh
  Line or code reference: Lines 198-212 (tracking-issue fallback extraction)
  Problem: When `--tracking-issue` is not provided, the script calls `_force_tick_fetch_issue_body` on the `--issue` argument and parses its body for the literal `Tracking issue: #NNNN` marker; if that marker is missing, `TRACKING_ISSUE` stays empty and the dispatch is skipped.
  Why it fails at runtime: The post-implement, post-review-blocked, and post-resolver-failed force tick never wakes the orchestrator poller because the tracking issue was never resolved.
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4
- File: scripts/render_prompt.sh
  Line or code reference: Lines 54, 57 (SEMBLE_PREFETCH and SERENA_TOOL_HINTS substitution)
  Problem: The substitution uses `${SEMBLE_PREFETCH_BLOCK%$'\n'}` which strips only the LAST trailing newline from a multiline value, unlike the old renderer’s exact trailing-newline behavior.
  Why it fails at runtime: A multi-paragraph prefetch block loses a separator blank line compared to `render_prompt.py`, which can affect prompt layout and LLM comprehension of section boundaries.
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 3
- File: scripts/orchestrate_force_tick.sh
  Line or code reference: Lines 267-282 (claim-put followed by peer re-read)
  Problem: The idempotency guard uses a two-phase pattern: `memory_force_tick_put` writes a pending record, then the function re-reads via `memory_force_tick_get` and checks cooldown again; there is no atomic compare-and-swap.
  Why it fails at runtime: Two concurrent phase-end runs can both observe no cooldown, both push their pending records, and both proceed to dispatch, violating the cooldown contract.
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4
- File: scripts/orchestrate_force_tick.sh
  Line or code reference: Line 234 (`FORCE_TICK_ENABLED` early exit)
  Problem: When `FORCE_TICK_ENABLED` evaluates to false, the script exits 0 immediately without consulting or writing any cooldown state.
  Why it fails at runtime: If the flag is toggled off and back on inside the same cooldown window, duplicate dispatches occur because the disable period left no persisted record.
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 3
- File: scripts/render_prompt.sh
  Line or code reference: Lines 32-80 (removal of `render_prompt.py` delegation and removal of `SCRIPT_DIR`, `PROMPT_BASENAME`, `MODE_NAME`, and `resolve_render_prompt_py` helpers)
  Problem: The old `render_prompt.sh` was a shim that delegated to `render_prompt.py`; the new `render_prompt.sh` is a self-contained bash renderer and the comment/documentation relationship no longer holds.
  Why it fails at runtime: Not a direct runtime failure, but a stale-artifact hazard: future maintainers who read the shim-documentation comments or add new contracts expecting them to be enforced will be surprised that validation is silently gone.
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 3
- Requirement: "Force-tick dispatch is idempotent per tracking issue within the cooldown window." (Acceptance criteria)
  Expected change site: scripts/orchestrate_force_tick.sh (specifically the claim-then-dispatch logic at lines 267-318)
  Evidence of absence: The implementation uses a git-push-based claim pattern (memory_force_tick_put) followed by a peer re-read (memory_force_tick_get) to detect races, but git pushes on the ai-memory branch are not an atomic compare-and-swap. Two concurrent processes can both observe no cooldown, both push pending records (second overwrites the first), and both dispatch. The test `test_force_tick_second_call_inside_cooldown_noops` tests only sequential calls with a single mock, not true concurrency.
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4
- Requirement: "Keep the matching listed workflow-template wrappers in sync where this issue already names them."
  Expected change site: workflow-templates/ai-implement.yml, workflow-templates/ai-review.yml, workflow-templates/ai-validate.yml
  Evidence of absence: The three workflow-template wrappers delegate to `.github/workflows/implement.yml`, `.github/workflows/review_autofix.yml`, and `.github/workflows/validate.yml` respectively at `@stable`. The force-tick changes are entirely internal to those called workflows — the templates pass through inputs/secrets and contain no polling, label, or dispatch logic that needs updating.
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5 (verified: no template changes needed)
- Requirement: "Tests cover cooldown/no-op behavior and the dispatch payload shape."
  Expected change site: tests/test_orchestrate_force_tick.py
  Evidence of absence: The test file covers the happy path (dispatch + state write), the cooldown no-op path (sequential), and the post-cooldown re-dispatch path. It does not cover: `FORCE_TICK_ENABLED=false` exit path, a failed git push to ai-memory (`memory_force_tick_put` returning `stored: false`), a failed `gh workflow run` (`dispatch_status=failed` branch), the resolver-failed invocation path, or a genuine concurrent race between two script invocations.
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 3
=== END FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-p
